anchors: the same system's earlier runs are a working peer in time
decision: For a fault seen once, read the same system's earlier runs (previous boots, earlier CI runs, older logs) as a working peer in time before proposing a lasting fix; if the good runs show the race normally won, the bad run had a separate cause.

evidence.text: Queued lesson: three earlier boots of the same host showed the race won by 0.5 to 2 s, so the one bad boot had a separate cause. Text-only RED probe on the pre-edit text answered NONE for earlier runs of the same system.

reopen_if: A case where the earlier runs of the same system cannot be read (no persistent journal, rotated CI logs) is common enough that the rule needs a fallback, or the rule is shown to delay a fix that the earlier runs could not have changed.
why: The skill's working-peer material compared only against a comparable host; a single bad run plus a timing observation led straight to a lasting ordering fix that earlier boots of the same host would have refuted.
